 <ns0:seg xml:id="hcc4-generated-000003" type="ThML-generalInfo">
  <ns0:seg xml:id="hcc4-generated-000004" type="ThML-description">Philip Schaff's <ns0:hi xml:id="hcc4-generated-000005" rend="italic">History of the Christian 
Church</ns0:hi> excels at providing an impressive and instructive 
historical treatment of the Christian church. This eight 
volume work begins with the early Church and ends at 1605 
with the Swiss Reformation. Schaff's treatment is 
comprehensive and in depth, discussing all the major (and 
minor!) figures, time periods, and movements of the 
Church. He includes many footnotes, maps, and charts; he 
even provides copies of original texts in his treatment. 
One feature of the <ns0:hi xml:id="hcc4-generated-000006" rend="italic">History of the Christian Church</ns0:hi> that 
readers immediately notice is just how beautifully written it 
is--especially in comparison to other texts of a similar nature. Simply 
put, Schaff's prose is lively and engaging. As one reader puts it, these 
volumes are "history written with heart and soul." Although at points 
the scholarship is slightly outdated, overall <ns0:hi xml:id="hcc4-generated-000007" rend="italic">History of the 
Christian 
Church</ns0:hi> is great for historical referencing. Countless people have 
found 
<ns0:hi xml:id="hcc4-generated-000008" rend="italic">History of the Christian Church</ns0:hi> useful. Whether for serious 
scholarship, 
sermon preparation, daily devotions, or simply edifying reading, 
<ns0:hi xml:id="hcc4-generated-000009" rend="italic">History 
of the Christian Church</ns0:hi> comes highly recommended.<ns0:lb xml:id="hcc4-generated-000010"/><ns0:lb xml:id="hcc4-generated-000011"/>Tim 
Perrine<ns0:lb xml:id="hcc4-generated-000012"/>CCEL 
Staff 
Writer </ns0:seg>
